messages.content:
Work out the ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category for the episode below. The principal diagnosis is the single condition established after investigation to be chiefly responsible for the patient's episode of admitted care. It is not the patient's most serious comorbidity, not the presenting symptom, and not the procedure performed.

Think in three steps: first name the condition chiefly responsible for the admission, second name the ICD-10-AM chapter letter it belongs to, third give the three-character category.

Example 1
Hospital course: A 72-year-old man with a 50 pack-year smoking history was admitted with three days of worsening breathlessness and purulent sputum. Spirometry showed an FEV1/FVC ratio of 0.52. He was treated with nebulised bronchodilators, oral prednisolone and antibiotics for an infective exacerbation of his long-standing airflow limitation.
Answer: Irreversible airflow limitation in a heavy smoker with an infective exacerbation is chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, chapter J, category J44.
CODE: J44

Example 2
Hospital course: A 58-year-old man presented with crushing central chest pain radiating to the jaw. The electrocardiogram showed ST elevation in the anterior leads and high-sensitivity troponin rose from 40 to 2100 ng/L. He underwent primary percutaneous coronary intervention with a stent to the proximal left anterior descending artery.
Answer: ST elevation with a rising troponin and culprit-vessel stenting is an acute myocardial infarction, chapter I, category I21.
CODE: I21

Hospital course:
Discharge Summary:

Patient Information:
Name: [Redacted]
Age: 53
Sex: Female
Date of admission: [Redacted]
Date of discharge: [Redacted]

Hospital Course:

The patient was admitted with a one-week history of abdominal pain, constipation, nausea, vomiting, and a single episode of bright red blood per rectum. Two days following her presentation, she developed bilateral facial weakness, perioral numbness, and difficulty in swallowing initiation. On examination, the patient had diminished bilateral facial musculature strength and an absent left patellar reflex. CT and MRI of the brain were obtained and showed changes consistent with chronic small vessel ischemic disease. Neurology was consulted and recommended a lumbar puncture which showed increased protein with absent white and red blood cells, raising the suspicion of Guillain-Barré syndrome. The patient was started on intravenous immunoglobulins and monitored in the progressive care unit. After a five-day course of IVIG, the patient showed a slight improvement but did not show up for her follow-up appointment and left against medical advice on day 9 of hospitalization.
Discharge Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Discharge Instructions:

The patient is advised to seek medical attention immediately if she experiences any new neurological symptoms such as numbness, tingling, or weakness in the extremities. She is also advised to attend all scheduled follow-up appointments and continue any prescribed medications as per the instructions of her primary care physician.

Write your reasoning in at most three short sentences, then a final line of exactly 'CODE: <letter><digit><digit>'.

text:
The condition chiefly responsible for this episode is Guillain-Barré syndrome. It presented as bilateral facial weakness, areflexia and dysphagia with albuminocytologic dissociation on CSF, was treated with IVIG, and the abdominal symptoms were a likely prodrome. This sits in chapter G (nervous system), category G61 (inflammatory polyneuropathy).

CODE: G61
